To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) users of an interactive cross-language information access system were able to answer 62% of factual questions from a collection of documents written primarily in a foreign language in an average of less than 3 minutes; 2) a single segment summary of the translated document was found to be as effective as a multi-paragraph summary of the translated text in an interactive cross-language question answering task; 3) the number of iterations of the query refinement process was positively correlated with question difficulty, and

(1) the use of a cross-language information access system can help users answer factual questions about a subject in which they have little proficiency, (2) users can benefit from interactive query reformulation and from the display of summaries, and (3) the type of summary used does not appear to affect performance.

the average user can answer 62% of factual questions about a large document collection written in a language that the user knows poorly, in 176 seconds per query, using a system that provides optional query translation and optional summaries of individual retrieved documents, and that users are not significantly more likely to find the correct answer when they are given a summary drawn from three segments of the translated documents rather than a single segment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of interactive techniques for information access in languages in which the user may have little proficiency.
the design and evaluation of interactive techniques for question answering from large document collections in cross-language information retrieval.
the problem of cross-language question answering.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interactive cross-language retrieval task is difficult and that users need assistance to be able to perform the task effectively.
the system was able to support a level of performance that would have been unachievable without the use of the interactive techniques described here.
the experimental system was not able to provide a satisfactory solution to the problem of answering questions about documents written in an unfamiliar language.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the interactive cross-language question answering task is very difficult, but the use of extractive summaries in an interactive system may improve the user's ability to find the correct answer.
the interactive system provided some assistance in the task, but that the users' performance was not as good as we had hoped.

, although users were not able to correctly answer a majority of the questions, they were able to do so in less than three minutes on average, and the system was able to assist users in finding the correct answers to a majority of the queries.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for this particular task, interactive query expansion was not helpful, but the use of extractive summaries drawn from multiple document segments, rather than from a single segment, did appear to improve the effectiveness of the cross-language retrieval system.
, in the case of interactive cross-language information access, the quality of the translation of the user's query is the most important factor in determining the quality of the user's experience.
interactive cross-language question answering is feasible and can be improved with better query formulation techniques.
